consul noun

Traupman 296

cōnsul, cōnsulis m.

noun, third declension

a consul, the head of a consulate

The medieval title of the officers who looked after merchants’ rights in foreign ports (Du Cange, in Morgan–Owens), and still the Latin for a consul, with the country or the city in the genitive or as an adjective. A Roman consul was head of the state (see consul, of ancient Rome); a modern one looks after his country’s citizens and trade in a foreign city, and ranks below an ambassador.

Other words

  • cōnsulis sēdēs — a consulate

    noun phrase: sēdēs with the genitive cōnsulis · also used · modern · M-O s.v. consulate

Examples

  • cōnsulis nostrī Smyrnae interventū

    through the good offices of our consul at SmyrnaTrappen (1843), in M-O s.v. consul

See also consul, embassy, ambassador, passport.
